subject: sweaty socks
title: What If You Never Changed Your Socks?

scenes.text: What if you never changed your socks? Your feet sweat more than you think.
Your two feet have about 250,000 sweat glands, and can make up to half a pint of sweat a day.
Skin bacteria feed on that sweat and make isovaleric acid, the cheesy smell of old socks.
Warm, damp socks suit the fungus behind athlete's foot, which affects up to one in four adults.
Keep feet wet and cold for as little as 10 to 14 hours and you risk trench foot. Over 20,000 British troops got it in 1914 and 1915.
The fix doctors still give is the same one: dry feet, and fresh socks at least once a day.
